subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.
reasoning:
Given the low effort budget, I'm thinking I should keep the module compact but still well-built—static parts without joints should work fine for this vehicle, so I'll skip rigging a turret and just model it as a simple static structure with rough dimensions around 9 meters long.

I'm sketching out the chassis, six wheels on three axles, a cab up front, and a railgun mounted above pointing forward, plus four outrigger stabilizer legs touching the ground. Now I'm planning the helper functions for boxes and cylinders, how to orient parts along different axes, and which color kits and glow textures to apply for the military olive panelling and rail lighting.

Writing wheel geometry...

Now I'm building the cab with a tilted windshield box, then constructing the main hull body and sketching the railgun turret ring with parallel rail bars on top, working out the overall vehicle length.

For the gun tilt, I'm computing a rotation about the X-axis so the barrel angles upward about 12 degrees over the cab, deriving the transformed y/z coordinates and deciding to compute world positions via a pivot-based function rather than nesting groups.

Writing gun geometry...

Adding coil rings around the rails and a glowing cyan plasma strip between them, plus a muzzle brake block with slots. Then I'm working out the turret mount with trunnion towers, a lathe-ring base, platform box, and stabilizer legs positioned at the corners.

Still placing legs... each has an outrigger arm, diagonal hydraulic strut, telescoping piston cylinder, and a hexagonal landing pad, with wheel positions set along the z-axis.

Confirming the leg placements clear the wheel gaps and the pad touches the floor correctly. Now I'm planning additional hull details: side armor panels, storage boxes between wheels, antenna mast, radar dish, light bar, exhaust stacks, and front/rear elements like bumpers, winch, tow hook, and glowing headlights/tail lights.

Adding cab hatch, searchlight, and camo paint patches, plus decal textures for roundels, stencil numbers, hazard chevrons, and warning labels. I'm defining helper functions for boxes, cylinders, and decals to streamline part creation.

Writing part helper functions...

I'm also adding textures like roundels, stencil text, hazard stripes, and warning labels using monospace fonts, then working out a camo paint pattern for the hull using a mottled olive and dark green blend.

For the hull paint, I'm layering a patch-based camo pattern with panel detailing and rivets, then adding a mud effect near the bottom based on surface position and lighting from above.

Checking the texel resolution against the model's scale, I realize standard seam widths would be too thin to render properly, so I'm writing a custom plated paint function with wider seams and a bevel highlight, plus wear effects like mud at the bottom and soot near the exhaust.

Still writing paint function...

Still defining wheel geometry...

Adding mud flaps, axle housings with differential bulges, leaf spring suspension, and a dark steel chassis frame with cross members and an underbelly skid plate.

Now I'm positioning the main hull box and checking clearances against the wheel fenders and arches, then placing the cab section above and forward of the hull.

The gun pivot sits elevated behind the cab, and I'm checking its trajectory at full elevation clears the cab roof with margin. I'm also adding beveled armor panels along the hull's upper edges using rotated thin boxes, though I need to work out the correct rotation sign so the chamfer slopes the right direction.

I'm now working out the windshield geometry -- a thin tilted box rotated about the X axis so its surface slants backward and its normal points upward and forward, settling on roughly -25 degrees.

Simplifying the cab dimensions to a single forward-control box with windshield band, grille plane at the lower front, glowing headlight boxes flanking the grille, and a bumper box beneath it.

I'm checking the wheel positions against the cab width to make sure the fenders don't clip through the cab geometry, adjusting narrower cab bounds so the wheel inner faces just clear the hull sides.

Then I'm planning the decal and detail layout: door stars, hull side stencils, hazard stripes at the rear, vent grilles on the hull sides, plus winch drum and tow hook cylinders near the bumper, before sketching a rear ramp plate.

Now I'm adding glowing red tail lights near the rear corners, a tow hitch, side storage bins along the hull, and twin exhaust stacks positioned behind the cab with flared lathe-style caps, checking they don't clash with the gun rails.

For the turret, I'm building a lathe-profile base ring, then stacking a turret box on top with trunnion towers on either side to hold the gun pivot, working out the heights so the gun rails and pivot point align properly without clipping into the turret top.

Verifying cab clearance against the gun at that height checks out. Now I'm detailing the gun's rail geometry with blued-steel boxes, copper inner strips, and a glowing plasma strip running between them.

Adding coil rings around the barrel...

Adding small clamp blocks per ring to secure them to the rails, then designing the breech section as a box covering the rear of the gun, and placing capacitor bank cylinders near the top rear for the power system.

Adding a muzzle ring and face, a trunnion pin with brass caps and lugs, elevation hydraulic cylinder rods linking turret to gun lugs, a top-mounted sight optic, and a rear antenna whip with tip light plus a radar dish on the turret.

Now I'm adding hull details: roof hatches, vents, rear stowage brackets, and tilted smoke dischargers on the turret sides, along with stabiliser legs including an arm box, diagonal brace rod, and vertical sleeve cylinder for support.

Adding leg pad details...

I'm sketching a hydraulic hose sweep from hull to sleeve, then an amber beacon glow on the cab roof dome. Counting textures needed (star, stencil, hazard, grille, screen, warn, chevron) and settling on metal paint finishes for the gun and rails using blued iron and steel.

Now I'm setting up the builder imports and scaffolding the box helper function for constructing the carrier geometry...

Adding gun geometry helpers...

Working out tire grime shading, lug nut placement around the wheel loop, fender geometry, mud flaps, and a small "RG-6" stencil decal with an outline for the badge SVG.

Now sketching remaining icon SVGs: a military-style star roundel with a pale circle and tan five-point star, a yellow-black hazard stripe pattern, a dark grille with horizontal slats, a screen readout with green "ARM" text, and a warning triangle icon with lightning bolt and "HV 40MJ" label. Planning to assemble all of this into the final compact code output.

I'm also working out the vehicle's radar dish geometry as a closed, non-self-intersecting profile, tilted on an angled axis and positioned at the turret rear, along with the mirror arms and mounting details. For the cab, I'm placing dark glass windows, a star decal near the door, and thin seam and handle details before finalizing everything and writing the complete code.
